decisions.reason: The explicit transition from a modular main board to one integrated board necessarily changes the board context for the retained ESP32 GPIO assignments.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Yes, I think they can, now that there is only one board + sensors/buttons/leds which are all easy to position I think there is no issue wherever you put them

decisions.reason: The existing same-message MODIFY already removes the obsolete modular-main-board context and retains the integrated-board and generic-platform contexts.
The existing same-message MODIFY already moves the pull-ups to the integrated board, removes the obsolete interboard cable-length attribute, and updates scope.
The source grants mechanical connector-placement flexibility but does not change the panel inputs, GPIO assignments, or connector-based mounting behavior.
The existing same-message MODIFY already records removal of the modular interboard interface and deletes the obsolete connector, pinout, and board-chain attributes.
The existing same-message MODIFY already removes the obsolete separate-power-board activation condition and moves the supply requirement to the integrated-board context.
The existing same-message MODIFY already changes the programming interface scope from the modular main board to the integrated board without altering the USB-C requirement.
The existing same-message MODIFY already updates the measurement coverage and scope for sensors and LEDs on the integrated board.
The existing same-message MODIFY already relocates the connector and PWRON connection to the integrated board and records the granted placement flexibility.
This requirement was already scoped to the integrated board, and connector-placement flexibility does not change its battery, USB, or power-path behavior.
The existing same-message MODIFY already converts the board role and sensor supply to the integrated design and removes obsolete main-board input connectors and the old total connector count.
The existing same-message MODIFY directly and completely records the client's permission to place connectors across the proposed board sides.
